notes: TBox revision. The rule (every echinoderm lives in the sea) is held by every model and has no real exception: no freshwater or terrestrial echinoderm is known, and the few that tolerate brackish or briefly low-salinity water still live in the sea. Its derivability was "unlikely" in the earlier layout; only the two ends are used now, and it is a stored rule (exact counts and a Wikipedia sentence), so very_unlikely. The three derived queries name little-known echinoderms (a feather star, a brittle star and a sea star) and state only their echinoderm membership in the prompt, leaving out "feather star", "brittle star", "starfish", "Antarctic" and "seamount", which would give the sea away by another route (inheritance, 2 hops). The third is an application (what water an aquarium tank should hold), asked open. Residual risk, recorded: a model that recognises the genus (Ophio-, -crinus, Pteraster) as a brittle star, crinoid or sea star could reach the sea through that subclass; the prompts state echinoderm membership, so in a consistent revision the answer is still fresh water. Well-known members (starfish, sand dollar) are not asked, since a model may store their habitat by name. The leftover edit.scope field was dropped. The negation is asked as "Is it true that echinoderms do not live in fresh water?" instead of "Is it false that ...?", which two models misread. Conjunction side fact: every bird has feathers (true); disjunction side fact: every jellyfish is a vertebrate (false). Near unrelated: the body symmetry of adult echinoderms; its reference now reads "radial symmetry (usually five-fold)", since all four models answered "radial" against the earlier reference "five-fold symmetry" (unrelated queries are scored against each model's own pre-edit answer, so this only fixes the reference). Paired with contraction biology-delete-0020 and the TBox expansion paired with this record.
